method: Viewed aligned full-frame and enlarged five-time-point motion sheets for all eight samples, then inspected 1.35s cropped covers at card size; checked alternating pixel counts for blink and pulse variants; machine command and export audits were completed separately.

decisions.observation: The sample reveals one Chinese character near 0.10s, a longer prefix at 0.45s, and the complete title by 0.85s; no scaling or flicker is substituted for letter reveal.
The orange title begins small and faint at 0.10s, reaches its full size near 0.45s, and stays steady; unlike the typewriter, all characters scale together.
The cyan title grows in together, remains legible at full size, then visibly shrinks and fades near 1.80s; the two-sided scale motion differs from the one-way burst.
The pink full title repeatedly expands and contracts after fading in. Its size and foreground area vary across the middle samples without losing the whole word.
The green title alternates between nearly invisible and readable states at a regular short interval; sampled foreground counts alternate between about 17 and 156 pixels.
The serif gold title starts with a single Chinese character, adds the rest in order, then expands rhythmically and shrinks on exit; both reveal and size motion are visible.
The purple full title grows in as one object, then alternates bright and dim while remaining in place, and shrinks at the end; no letter-by-letter reveal occurs.
The cyan and magenta title reveals characters progressively, then switches between bright and dim states; its reveal plus opacity rhythm differs from the gold pulse variant.
